definition: A model in which all parameters are used for every input, as opposed to sparse architectures that activate only a subset.
details: Most traditional transformer language models are dense, meaning the full network is engaged for every token processed, which becomes increasingly costly to run as model size grows.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. Boil it down and it is this: A model in which all parameters are used for every input, as opposed to sparse architectures that activate only a subset. Here is why it matters: Most traditional transformer language models are dense, meaning the full network is engaged for every token processed, which becomes increasingly costly to run as model size grows. The shape of the machine is half the idea. That blueprint is Dense Model.
